Subject: Exploring vendor replacement economics and incentives

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the call last week. We're moving through an internal vendor refresh and have a competing commercial that looks aggressive on headline pricing. Procurement asked me to reach out to see what creative retention levers Redwood can put on the table — specifically we care about minimizing near-term cash outlay while keeping runtime parity and a clean migration path.

Can you share:
- A short list of incentive constructs you typically provide (credits, rebates, implementation vouchers)
- Any limits on how credits can be applied (eg, egress, prepay, billing offsets)
- A sample SOW or DocuSign flow for a pilot + migration phase

I've attached the competitor term sheet for context (redacted). Procurement will prefer credits over permanent list-price discounts if the NPV is roughly equivalent.

Appreciate a quick reply — our buying committee meets next Tuesday (Dec 8).

Best,
Allyson Park

Hi Allyson,

Thanks — got the term sheet and appreciate the clarity on procurement's preference. High level: we can structure a two-phase credit weave that aligns near-term cash neutrality with a longer runway of consumption-based offsets to reduce your run-rate risk.

Two quick constructs we commonly propose:
1) Onboarding credit (one-time): covers integration egress and first 30 days of peak traffic; paid as a bill credit applied after go-live.
2) Sustained ramp credit (tiered monthly offsets): a 3–6 month schedule that phases down as usage reaches agreed baselines.

We can also do an upfront partial prepay + smaller monthly credits if finance prefers a simpler single-line item. Credits are typically applied against usage invoices; they cannot be transferred, but we can make carveouts so credits cover egress or dedicated pool spend first.

I'm attaching a very rough incentive matrix so you can see how the numbers ladder. If you can share a 3-month usage profile (token mix, peak windows, expected qps), I'll run a custom NPV comparison against the competitor's delta.

Would you be available for a 30-min walkthrough on Friday (Dec 5) or Monday (Dec 8) ahead of your committee meeting?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Attachment: initial_incentive_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Marissa / Grace — forwarding Allyson's email and the term sheet. Key points from my take: procurement wants credits (not permanent discount) and will prioritize low near-term cash. They care about runtime parity and a clean migration.

Proposed internal approach (high level):
- Offer A (two-phase credit weave):
  * Onboarding credit = $150k one-time invoice credit to cover egress + integration (applied after go-live).
  * Ramp credits = $40k/month for 4 months (stepped: 40/30/20/10) applied to usage invoices.
  * Technical carveout: 90-day runtime parity warranty on core text-gen models; fallback to tiered compatible variant if capacity constrained.
- Offer B (simple prepay + rebate):
  * $200k upfront prepaid credit applied to first 12 months usage; no separate ramp credits.

Risks / constraints:
- Finance wants to cap total concession at ~$300k ARR-equivalent over 12 months unless AE gets manager signoff.
- Legal wants a narrow warranty language; cannot promise explicit SLAs outside our standard SLA schedule without an enterprise addendum.
- Ops needs a clearly defined roll-off and telemetry checkpoint for credits (we recommend monthly usage attestation and a 30-day remediation window).

Next steps: can you confirm what upper bound we can approve without exec sign-off? Also need input on how strictly we should tie onboarding credit to egress vs general usage.

Thanks,
Mina

Appreciate the clarity and the procurement constraints. Attached are two concise artifacts: a one-page two-phase term sheet and a redlineable SOW for pilot + migration. High-level commercial summary below (numbers intended to be illustrative and flexible pending usage profile):

Commercial proposal (Option A — two-phase credit weave):
- Onboarding credit (one-time invoice credit): $150,000 — explicitly earmarked to cover egress and 60 days of third-party licensing costs; applied after go-live as a credit line on the invoice.
- Ramp/tiered credits: $40,000 / month for months 1–4, stepping down to $20,000 month 5 and $10,000 month 6 (total ramp credits = $160,000). Credits are invoice offsets and expire after month 6.
- Total nominal concession = $310,000.
- We will provide SOC 2 type II report and a technical appendix documenting runtime parity expectations.

Alternative (Option B — single prepay):
- Prepaid credit: $250,000 applied to first 12 months of usage. No additional ramp credits.
- Total nominal concession = $250,000.

Operational guardrails:
- Telemetry checkpoint at month 2 and month 4 to validate usage and parity metrics. If parity regressions are confirmed, we will: (a) accelerate ramp credits for 30 days while Ops remediate, or (b) open a fallback path to a compatible model variant.
- Legal: include standard limitation of liability and an explicit carveout that credits only apply to invoiced usage (not third-party professional services beyond the SOW unless explicitly listed).

Ask: please confirm which option procurement prefers and attach the 3-month token/usage profile you mentioned. If you want our finance team to produce an NPV calc, we'll need the usage projection by COB Monday (Dec 14 PST).
